Help test the research preview

Try one simulation, flag a missing paper or propose a calibration dataset.

A ten-minute walkthrough

  1. Open the TPMET circuit laboratory. With the demonstration defaults, note the resting voltage of about −71.241 mV.
  2. Change the uncompensated fraction η from 0.5 to 0. Net TPMET current should become zero, and resting voltage should become about −74.815 mV.
  3. Reset the demo, then double capacitance from 20 to 40 pF. Resting voltage should stay the same, the time constant should double and the cutoff frequency should halve.
  4. Inspect the hypotheses and export a JSON record. Decide what experimental result would contradict one of them.
  5. Search the literature collection for a paper you know. Record its DOI or PMID if missing.

These expected values test the implemented equations. They are not observed cancer-cell measurements.

What feedback is most useful?

  • Physics or units — specify the input values, expected result and actual result.
  • Scientific interpretation — identify the unsupported inference or missing assumption.
  • Literature — supply a DOI or PMID and why the study is relevant.
  • Usability — describe the browser, device and steps that failed.
  • Calibration — describe cell type, treatments, biological replicates, electrical measurements and biological endpoints. Share only data you are authorised to share.

Send feedback to Frankie Rawson. The link opens your email application. This page does not upload or store feedback.

Research status

Default parameters are illustrative. Cancer-outcome hypotheses are unvalidated. Literature records await screening and the collection is not exhaustive. Model identifier passive-tpmet-circuit-1.0.
